prompt: Which rider habit does the motorcycle operator manual call a frequent factor in crashes involving motorcyclists?
choices: Riding with the headlight on in daylight
Using both brakes for every stop
Riding in the left third of the lane
explanation: "Following too closely" is a frequent factor in crashes involving motorcyclists. A motorcycle needs as much distance to stop as a car, so keep at least a two-second gap, and more when conditions are poor. The other choices are habits the manual recommends.
ref: MSF Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 15 (Following Another Vehicle)
